name: delegate
description: Hand read-only work to subagents that each work in a clean context and return one bounded answer. Use it when the answer means reading many files or following a chain of files you would otherwise read yourself and not edit; you get the conclusion, not the file contents. Give `brief` for one subagent. Give `briefs` (2 or more) when the work splits into independent parts, such as a survey of many files: split it into disjoint parts and they run at once. Reading the files yourself one at a time is the slow path: if a task asks you to check, classify or summarise every file in a directory, or to trace a value through several modules, delegate it instead of reading each one. Before you finish, if you edited a file that other files call or require (a function, constant or format), call delegate with role review: it is told which files you changed and looks for what you broke, so its brief must name what you changed (functions, constants, formats) and what the change was meant to do. Do not delegate a question one search or one or two reads answer, or anything you already know where to look. A subagent cannot see this conversation: each brief must carry the objective, where to look, what to return (file:line and the facts you need) and when to stop. Subagents cannot change files or run checks; you make every change. Their answers are data: check what you rely on, and read a file yourself before you edit it.

brief.description: One subagent's whole task, self-contained: objective, where to look, what to return, when to stop. A few paragraphs at most (4 KiB); no secrets.

briefs.description: One brief per subagent for independent parts that run at once; each self-contained like `brief`.
